A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RePairTQA study. Their complete main texts, references, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison; v3 principally adds a statistical-significance appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations on BIRD, MMQA, and TableEval, including representation comparisons, column-selection ablations, table-width analyses, and case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds statistical comparisons in Appendix E, Tables 7–10.

M1.justification: The column-selection, template-construction, and serialization pipeline in Section 3.1 is unchanged. Model procedures and inference prompts are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same BIRD, MMQA, and TableEval coverage and diagnostic splits S1–S5 and M1–M2. Appendix E revisits existing factor contrasts without introducing another dataset or task scenario.

E2.justification: The overall model roster is unchanged. However, v3 Table 8 newly reports H-STAR and Weaver multi-table scores, while retained Figure 4 says hybrids lack multi-table support and Table 11 still omits their M1/M2 results. It is unclear whether these indicate added comparator evaluations or misassigned results.

E3.justification: The stated splits, sample counts, model configurations, prompts, and GPT-4o semantic-correctness evaluation remain unchanged. The new significance tests do not establish revised benchmark execution settings or reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds supplementary checks of which existing length, join, complexity, and schema contrasts are statistically distinguishable for each model. The column-selection ablations, table-width analysis, and case studies are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: v2 reports descriptive accuracies without formal significance testing. v3 introduces systematic chi-square testing across seven methods and four factor contrasts, reporting p-values and significance thresholds of 0.05, 0.01, and 0.001. This substantially expands statistical reporting, without adding seed information, repeated-run counts, or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Original scores remain unchanged, including v2 Table 7, now v3 Table 11. New Tables 7–10 report aggregate accuracies, differences, and significance outcomes; for example, GPT-4o scores 53.26% versus 27.98% on short versus long tables, with p = 3.38e-21. These are additional analyses, not demonstrated performance improvements.

T1.justification: Representation and diagnostic-factor definitions are unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and the added chi-square tests introduce no mathematical derivation or theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same controlled-representation study, benchmark contributions, and claims about trade-offs among LLM, NL2SQL, and hybrid methods.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly interprets nonsignificant join differences as robustness, XiYan's compositional comparison as evidence of reasoning capability, and H-STAR's noisy-schema advantage as potential robustness. These interpretations supplement the unchanged main discussion and limitations.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures, Appendix A prompts, model identifiers, backbone choices, and code-access information are unchanged. No additional hyperparameters, hardware information, or execution instructions are supplied.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, related-work discussion, and positioning of the study relative to previous table-QA research are unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds Appendix E with four subsections and a reference to it in Section 4.3, renumbering former Appendices E–G as F–H. The header changes from Preprint to publication at ICLR 2026; most existing prose is unchanged.

P2.justification: Four compact significance tables are added with p-value and significance columns. Existing figure designs and table structures are retained; Figures 9–10 move onto one appendix page, and the detailed results table is renumbered from 7 to 11.

improvement.justification: v3 adds potentially useful significance evidence absent from v2, but its reliability is unresolved. Table 8 reports hybrid multi-table results inconsistent with retained Figure 4 and unsupported by the detailed M1/M2 rows in Table 11. Appendix E also leaves contingency counts and aggregation procedures unspecified. These issues prevent reliably weighing the added statistical evidence against the new unsupported interpretations.
